threads.body: Same issue as the WebMVC 6.0 module: `test` excludes `**/boot/**` and `**/filter/**`, but `testControllerTelemetry` doesn’t narrow its scope to those tests. This likely causes duplicate execution of most tests and does not guarantee the excluded tests run only under the specialized configuration. Add `include(\"**/boot/**\", \"**/filter/**\")` (or an equivalent filter) to `testControllerTelemetry` to ensure the split is effective.

As written, `test` excludes `**/boot/**` and `**/filter/**`, but `testControllerTelemetry` does not include only those excluded tests (it will run the full test suite again). This risks both (a) running many tests twice and (b) not actually isolating the excluded tests as intended. Consider adding `include(\"**/boot/**\", \"**/filter/**\")` to `testControllerTelemetry` (and optionally excluding those patterns from other custom Test tasks) so the excluded tests are run exactly once under the controller-telemetry JVM args.

The list items under `telemetry:` appear to be indented at the same level as the `telemetry:` key. In YAML, sequence items must be indented under their parent key (e.g., `telemetry:` then `  - when: ...`). As shown, this is likely invalid YAML and may break doc generation/parsing. Indent the `- when:` entries (and their nested blocks) one level deeper under `telemetry:`.

threads.body: `test` excludes `**/server/**` and `testControllerTelemetry` includes only `**/server/**`, but `testStableSemconv` does not exclude `**/server/**`. That means server tests will run at least twice (controller telemetry task + stable semconv task), increasing CI time and potentially mixing intended test matrices. If the intent is to mirror the WebFlux split, update `testStableSemconv` to `exclude(\"**/server/**\")` and (if needed) introduce a dedicated `testControllerTelemetryStableSemconv` task for `**/server/**` + stable semconv.
